# The Student Founder

> The Student Founder: Why Your Student Years Are the Best Time to Build Something Real. A book by Andrew Ashur, founder and CEO of Lucid Bots. Cover line: "How to start a real business as a student." Cover tagline: "Trying is free. It won't stay that way." Brand tagline: "$42 in the bank. No permission slip."

The book is a practical manual for high school students, college students, and recent graduates who want to build something real while trying still costs almost nothing. Its argument: as a student, the downside of building something real is close to nothing and the upside is uncapped, and it won't stay that way. The book measures agency as the Agency Quotient: the time between "I should" and "I am," counted as the days between having an idea and doing the first thing about it that a stranger could react to. Smaller is better, and the best count is zero.

Status: manuscript complete, advance reader's copy exists, publication February 2027. Readers can read chapter one free and leave an email at https://www.thestudentfounder.com to be notified at launch.

## Pages

- [Home](https://www.thestudentfounder.com/): the book, the Agency Quotient question, the Founder's Page, author bio, FAQ, and launch-list signup.
- [Press kit](https://www.thestudentfounder.com/press.html): book facts, bios, images, lines from the book, interview topics, and contact.
- [Chapter one: Blood in the Shoes](https://www.thestudentfounder.com/prologue.html): the full first chapter, free, on the page or as a PDF (https://www.thestudentfounder.com/the-student-founder-chapter-one.pdf). The two-mile walk across Chicago with forty-two dollars in the company account and the CEO on the twenty-eighth floor who said yes.
- [How to start a business in college](https://www.thestudentfounder.com/how-to-start-a-business-in-college.html): why a campus is the cheapest place to try, what founders who fail keep, the stop line (dollars and months set in advance), and the two rules (stay alive, generate revenue).
- [How to find a startup idea in college](https://www.thestudentfounder.com/how-to-find-a-startup-idea-in-college.html): boring industries, the vitamin-or-painkiller test, the one-week friction log, and asking for commitments instead of compliments.
- [How to get your first customers as a student](https://www.thestudentfounder.com/how-to-get-first-customers-as-a-student.html): research calls framed as a student, the discovery questions, demos over decks, micro-niches of 50 to 200 people, and a written test for real demand.
- [How to find time to start a business in college](https://www.thestudentfounder.com/how-to-find-time-to-start-a-business-in-college.html): A weekly budget of hours, protecting your sharpest hours, and scripting the week on Sunday.
- [How to choose a co-founder in college](https://www.thestudentfounder.com/how-to-choose-a-co-founder-in-college.html): The three questions, the four-week test, vesting and cliffs, and settling the split early.
- [How to build your first product as a student](https://www.thestudentfounder.com/how-to-build-your-first-product-as-a-student.html): Building with no engineering background, shipping an ugly first version, and what to test before you build.
- [How to charge and close your first customers](https://www.thestudentfounder.com/how-to-charge-and-close-your-first-customers.html): Charging from day one, following up, the objections you will hear, and deciding to build, pivot or kill.
- [How to market a student startup](https://www.thestudentfounder.com/how-to-market-a-student-startup.html): Building in public, picking one place, and the two numbers to track for your first ninety days.
- [How to fund a student startup](https://www.thestudentfounder.com/how-to-fund-a-student-startup.html): Bootstrapping or raising, the default-alive math, first investors with no network, and dilution.
- [The Agency Quotient](https://www.thestudentfounder.com/agency-quotient.html): definition, a worked example, and a tool to take your own count.
- [Books for student founders](https://www.thestudentfounder.com/reading-list.html): the eleven-book reading list from the book's appendix.
- [The Founder's Page](https://www.thestudentfounder.com/founders-page.html): the book's one-page business plan for students, printable.

## Contents of the book

- Part I, The Asymmetric Degree: Blood in the Shoes (chapter one), The Odds, The Trap and the Trade.
- Part II, The First Rep: How Do I Find an Idea?, How Do I Find the Time?, Who Do I Build With?
- Part III, The Compounding Loop: How Do I Find Customers?, How Do I Build the Product?, How Do I Close Customers?, How Do I Get People to Notice?
- Part IV, Pouring Fuel: How Do I Build a Team?, How Do I Fund It?
- Conclusion: The Startup Is You. The 30-Day Execution Sprint. Appendix.
- The Founder's Page: a one-page plan the reader fills in, line zero first, then one line per chapter.

## Author

Andrew Ashur is the founder and CEO of Lucid Bots, the world's largest provider of drones and robots for exterior cleaning. In 2025, Inc. 5000 named Lucid Bots the fastest-growing robotics manufacturer in the United States. He started it in college with a $12 soldering iron. Forbes 30 Under 30, Manufacturing & Industry (2021). Y Combinator S19. He served as Davidson College's Innovator-in-Residence, working with hundreds of student entrepreneurs. With his wife he co-founded Persto, mentorship program management software for venture mentoring programs. Personal site: https://www.andrewashur.com
